title: The Asset of the Free Port
premise: Kestrel Montrose, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Consulate—a diplomatic fiction that exists only in filing cabinets—receives a debt notice for a favor he never performed, signed with his own dead sister's handwriting. The stranger behind it is Ilse Varga, a former colleague presumed killed in a free-port warehouse fire that was actually a cover for a weapons shipment now bound for a staged 'accident' at a harbor summit. As Kestrel unravels who forged his signature and why, he realizes the consulate itself sanctioned the attack to bury its own laundering trail. In the end, Kestrel chooses justice over survival: he exposes the operation at the cost of his invisibility, burning his identity and vanishing into the same free port that once sheltered him.
about_author: Quentin Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent six years documenting the gray economies of duty-free ports before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a rotating series of harbor cafés, insisting that the best plots are overheard, not invented.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine document burn at the consulate is interrupted by an envelope containing a debt ledger in his dead sister's handwriting, itemizing a favor from 2014 he never performed. His handler dismisses it; Kestrel can't. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the first crack in ten years of carefully maintained invisibility.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and Ilse Varga, alive and hiding in the free port's no-man's-land. She reveals the fire was staged and the 'favor' was Kestrel's forged authorization of a weapons manifest. He must help her stop the summit attack or she releases the ledger, destroying him. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: The Accident Schedule
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, racing through the consulate's archives at night. He discovers the attack on the harbor summit was approved internally—to erase evidence of the consulate's own laundering—and that his handler authored both the forgery and the fire order. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into cold resolve as the clock ticks toward the scheduled 'accident.'

chapters.title: Free Port
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, dual POV converging at the docks. Kestrel and Ilse divert the shipment and broadcast the ledger to every delegation at the summit, sacrificing their cover forever. His handler is arrested by the very governments the consulate pretended to serve. Kestrel walks into the free port crowd, unnamed. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into freedom—the price of survival finally paid in full.
